summary: The synthetic set is not a Kaggle dataset. It is the OUTPUT of the public kernel josefreitasalvesneto/biohub-synthetic-dataset, made by José Freitas (the task text credits hengck23, but he only commented). Attach it as kernel_sources and it appears at /kaggle/input/biohub-synthetic-dataset/biohub_synthetic/. Size is 18.50 GB: 1,539 static volumes at native (64,256,256) uint16 with centroids, 12.03 GB; and 2,174 six-frame sequences, 6.47 GB. Each sequence holds volumes (6,64,64,64) uint16 STRIDE-pooled in XY, plus nodes [t,z,y,x,lineage_id] in native voxels, edges, and divisions (parent node ids). In total there are 165,267 divisions in 4,056,226 nodes. The licence is CC0 per the post only. I downloaded and inspected four sample files. The only thing WE could train on it before the deadline is our DaughterNet, the division-insertion ranker. The secondary and the detector are out: an epoch of the secondary takes 2.1 h; imissher got -0.006..-0.009 LB with a synthetic-adapted secondary; synthetic pretraining inflates node count; our fine-tune swaps are 0/4 on the LB. The DaughterNet recipe: build crops from ~900 sequences, pretrain ~20 min on a T4, run a zero-shot gate on the real pool rows, fine-tune the v1 recipe from that init (5 folds, ~25-30 min on 2xT4), then run the OOF and lab gates. It enters K2 through a 'divswap' weight-dataset swap, a copy of secswap's fail-loud sha pin, with zero added hidden runtime. Honest budget: 3-4 h of development, ~1.5-2 GPU-h plus a ~0.5 h dummy, 1-2 h of CPU lab, 7-10 h of wall time. It CAN make the 29 Sep 00:05Z W4 wave if a dedicated worker starts by ~08:00Z; the last start with any slack is ~13:00Z. But the mechanism barely transfers. Synthetic divisions are two re-rendered ellipsoids at 7.24±1.6 um, with no mitotic appearance, no appearance identity between frames, no broken-track confounders, and stride instead of our mean pooling. External evidence is 0 for 4 (1st place no gain; Juan Neira 0.910 -> 0.906 with a synthetic division gate; imissher -0.006..-0.009; hikaggler hold-out only). Freitas's own '0.960' is unverified and comes with no details. E[public] ~ -0.001..+0.001, P(>= +0.001) ~15%. Nothing here reaches R8-grade evidence. Recommendation: NO-GO for a slot or a final. If the user wants the flier anyway, run only the cheapest kill gate (G1, zero-shot on real pool rows, ~0.7 GPU-h, answer by ~10:00Z), and spend a W4 slot only if G1 and G2 both pass.

findings.what: Exact location and format of the 732103 synthetic set. It is NOT a Kaggle dataset: `kaggle datasets list --user josefreitasalvesneto` shows only an unrelated signature set. It is the output of kernel josefreitasalvesneto/biohub-synthetic-dataset (id_no 129280459; last run 2026-08-01 01:39Z; 26,290 s CPU). Attach it with kernel_sources: ["josefreitasalvesneto/biohub-synthetic-dataset"] and it mounts at /kaggle/input/biohub-synthetic-dataset/biohub_synthetic/{static,sequences}/. Size: 18.50 GB = static 1,539 x vol_NNNNN.npz (volume (64,256,256) uint16 at NATIVE resolution, centroids (N,3) float32 with sub-voxel precision, voxel_um (1.625,0.40625,0.40625); 12.03 GB, ~8.4 MB each) + sequences 2,174 x seq_NNNN.npz (volumes (6,64,64,64) uint16 STRIDE-pooled in XY; nodes (N,5) float32 [t,z,y,x,lineage_id] in NATIVE voxels, where lineage_id is shared by both daughters and so is not a track id; edges (E,2) int32; divisions = parent node ids; 6.47 GB, ~3.1 MB each). 165,267 divisions / 4,056,226 nodes (4.07% vs ~0.26% real); 47-147 divisions per sequence. Licence: CC0, stated in the post only; a kernel output carries no licence field. Author: José Freitas, NOT hengck23 (hengck23 only commented). It was calibrated on the first 10 videos of ONE embryo (by[embs[0]][:10], likely 44b6), shell_kind 'plane', real count range 140-417 per field.

findings.action: Correct the round key facts: the author is José Freitas, not hengck23, and the slug is a kernel output, not a dataset. Any training kernel must use kernel_sources, not dataset_sources. Read only the sequences/ subfolder (6.47 GB); the static volumes have no lineage.

findings.what: The generator's division model does not contain the cue our division ranker needs. In cell 15 a division replaces the parent at t+1 with two ellipsoids placed +-0.5*N(7.24, 1.6) um along a random direction. Every frame is re-rendered with a fresh RNG (default_rng(900000+j*97+t)), so a nucleus has no appearance identity over time and there is no mitotic appearance at all (no condensation, rounding or brightness change). There are no detector errors, so no broken continuations, and cells never enter or leave (positions are clipped). The frames are STRIDE-pooled, while our DaughterNet contract MEAN-pools XY by 4 (tools/daughternet.py l.5-6, l.30), so synthetic crops are noisier than what DaughterNet sees. What transfers is geometry only: 'a new cell appears ~7 um from a cell that is still there'. That is exactly the cue the real data confounds with broken continuations: the orphan median is 8.5-10 um against a 7.24 um sister separation (Lê Quang Cảnh, 732103), and real parent-to-daughter steps are 8.47 um median, 5.7-13.7 um range. Precision on the REAL candidate pool is DaughterNet's known weak point (v2 raised pool AUC 0.825 -> 0.875 and was still WORSE for insertion; CONTEXT l.1314-1322).

findings.what: SYN-DN, the only synthetic training that fits before 29 Sep 00:00Z. Pretrain DaughterNet (same build_model, the 3-class parent/daughter/cont on the DivNet contract) on synthetic sequences, then fine-tune on the real v1 samples and swap the 5 fold weights into the current BASE's insertion stage. RECIPE: (S0, ~45-60 min dev) new kernel 'kdn-synth' = kdn-train v3 cells + one synthetic-sample cell. kernel_sources = josefreitasalvesneto/biohub-synthetic-dataset; read seq_0000-0899 (~2.8 GB). Labels: parent = division ids with t in {1,2} (lags -1..+2 must stay inside frames 0-5, and the daughters at t+1 in {2,3} as well); daughter = the parent's edge targets at their first frame; cont = in-1/out-1 nodes with no division within 2 frames in their lineage. Take ~40k parent / 40k daughter / 80k cont. Coordinates: (z, y/4, x/4) on the pooled frame, BIG crop 18x34x34, per-frame percentile 50/99.5 normalisation clipped to [-0.5, 6], the Gaussian marker, and the kdn_core flips/rot90/jitter/gain. (S1, GPU ~15-20 min) Pretrain one model, AdamW lr 1e-3 cosine, ~6 epochs (~1M sample-iterations; v1 managed ~510k in ~8 min per fold on a T4). (G1, ~2 min, in the same kernel) Zero-shot: score the real rows of experiments/l2_daughternet/pool_samples.parquet (11,117 predicted-coordinate candidates) and the 17,143 GT rows. (S2, ~15 lines + a test in kdn_core: env KDN_INIT=<pretrained.pt> loads the state_dict before training) Fine-tune with the v1 recipe on GT rows only (K2 ships v1; v2 lost on insertion), lr 3e-4, 30 epochs, early stopping, same 5 folds and 44b6 leak groups: ~8 min crop cache + ~20-25 min on 2xT4. (G2) OOF readout plus the insertion replay lab. (S3, ~1 h dev + tests) Private dataset vitaliineibauer/biohub-kdn-synth-v1 with the 5 fold .pt files under vitalii_daughternet/. New builder patch 'divswap', a copy of secswap: it attaches the dataset and sets BIOHUB_DIVINS_WEIGHTS=/kaggle/input/biohub-kdn-synth-v1/vitalii_daughternet/*.pt. It must pin that path, because the default glob /kaggle/input/**/vitalii_daughternet/*.pt would ALSO match the v1 files in biohub-ft-weights, which stays attached. Fail loud if the match count differs from the v1 count or any path is outside the pinned dataset, and print the sha256 of each file. (S4) Build expSYN = BASE (exp70g, or whatever the W2/W3 reads make BASE) + --patch divswap with every other knob unchanged; dummy ~25-30 min. MECHANISM: 165k geometric division examples might sharpen the parent-vs-cont and daughter-as-v scores (daughter-as-v is the weakest link at 0.68). EXPECTED GAIN (arithmetic): K2 inserts up to DIVINS_CAP (6) forks per clip, ~29 public clips -> <= ~174 insertions, and only those on annotated lineages score. Calibration: cap 4 -> 6 (~+58 insertions at base precision) gave +0.002 public (~+1 net TP). One public TP ~ +0.002-0.003 and one scored FP ~ -0.001 (J_pub ~0.36-0.40, 0.1 weight). A ranker swap moves roughly +-1-2 scored events: E[public] ~ -0.001..+0.001, spread +-0.003, P(>= +0.001) ~15%, P(<= -0.001) ~30-35%. Priors: synthetic division models are 0 for 4 in public reports, and our fine-tune swaps are 0/4 on the LB. RUNTIME on the ~100-clip hidden run: +0 (same architecture, same number of models, same crops; inside K2's 7.4-7.8 h). BUDGET: dev ~3-4 h, GPU ~1.5-2 h (smoke + full) + ~0.5 h dummy out of ~9.5 h left, CPU lab 1-2 h, wall 7-10 h. Started 07:30-08:00Z, it is ready ~15:00-18:00Z, in time for the W4 wave (29 Sep 00:05Z; score ~07:30-08:30Z 29 Sep, before the 19:00Z finals read). Latest start with slack: ~13:00Z 28 Sep. After ~15:00Z it cannot make the 00:00Z dummy with any margin for one ERROR rebuild.

findings.action: DECISION for the main session: recommend NO-GO for a slot or a final (mechanism mismatch R24SY-2, prior evidence R24SY-4). If the user wants the flier (aggressive mode), give it to ONE dedicated worker and run S0+S1+G1 only (~1-1.5 h wall, ~0.7 GPU-h). Continue past G1 only on a pass. PRE-REGISTERED GATES (write them to CONTEXT before any number is read): G1 (kill) = zero-shot parent-vs-cont AUC on the real pool rows >= 0.70 AND daughter-vs-cont >= 0.60 (the dorado-only model reached 0.62/0.53 and was killed); else STOP. G2 = fine-tuned 5-fold OOF on the pool block beats v1 (parent 0.825, daughter-as-v per the v1 readout) by >= +0.03 on BOTH embryos separately, AND the replay lab on CONFIRMATION (135 videos, OOF p, cap 6, threshold re-set by eligible-count matching to v1) gives net TP >= v1 + 3 with added-fork precision >= 0.31 (CONTEXT l.1297-1310 floor). The lab base graph is exp39, not x138 (caveat: in-sample for the linker). G3 dummy = validate ok, 0 errors, DIVINS ENABLED with the new sha256 lines and a model count equal to v1's, node rows identical to the BASE dummy (insertion adds edges, not nodes), forks within +-30% of the BASE dummy (exp70g: 81), runtime <= 1,920 s. Only G1+G2+G3 PASS earns a W4 public probe, public-only, never a final (retrained model, no held-out LB gate; same caveat as the SEC files).

findings.what: The rest of the synthetic route was ruled out on time or evidence, with numbers so it is not re-proposed. (a) n2a/secondary fine-tune on the static volumes: one epoch of the secondary is 2.1 h on a T4 (exp71). The static volumes are native-resolution, but their centroids label every nucleus while the real GT is ~2.8% sparse, so the density and node-count calibration shift (the node-inflation risk hikaggler reports; exp23-type -0.007 at +0.62% nodes). Plus 1 dataset + secswap build + dummy ~0.5 h and a public-only read. Net: ~3-4 h GPU of ~9.5 h, E ~ -0.003 given imissher's -0.006..-0.009. NO. (b) Detector fine-tune: same evidence; Lê Quang Cảnh's sparse fine-tune lost 0.016 adj_J; our weight swaps are 0/4. NO. (c) Using the synthetic sister-separation to tune the insertion geometry gate is circular: 7.24 um is a generator constant fitted to the real lineage, and our 151 real GT divisions already constrain it. NO.

findings.what: Honest bottom line for the finals: nothing on the synthetic route reaches R8-grade evidence before 29 Sep. The best case is one public-only W4 read of SYN-DN at ~08:00Z 29 Sep, with a 0.001-level effect on ~20-40 annotated public divisions. That is inside the +-0.003 LB noise, cannot be separated from luck, and must not displace a W4 slot that currently holds a better-prior candidate (exp86a/b/c knob branches, the cap ladder, E10 copies). Freitas's 0.960 is a reason to read his write-up after 30 Sep, not to act now.
